name: StillPoint

temporal_authority.governing_rule: A successful description must not acquire permanent jurisdiction over the thing it describes.
enforced: claims and predictions do not self-authorize actions
warrants are domain, action, scope, and time bounded
expired, revoked, completed, superseded, released, or review-required warrants cannot authorize execution
material later evidence can force supporting authority into review
cross-domain claim use requires an explicit bridge
historical claims and evidence survive supersession and release
terminal runtime warrants are not silently reissued under the same authority revision
approval cannot revive a non-current temporal warrant
warrant changes during adapter execution prevent false completion
re-entry creates a new auditable evaluation rather than rewriting prior state
founder, administrator, and provider identity do not bypass warrant state
operationalized: operator CLI for claims, evidence, warrants, warrant events, and re-entry
explicit factual-claim binding for pending ActionRequests
claim-binding changes invalidate prior approval and require CEO reapproval
material continuing evidence propagates across task boundaries
live actions whose factual support enters review move to review_required and block their tasks
completed actions remain completed history while dynamic subjects may open a new re-entry evaluation
static subjects do not auto-open re-entry merely because later contradictory evidence exists

known_limitations: Production external adapters remain intentionally disabled; approved work without a live adapter still stops at ready_for_action.
Re-entry evaluation is durable and inspectable, but domain-specific policy still decides whether a new warrant should actually be issued.
A warrant invalidated during a real adapter call cannot undo an external side effect already emitted; StillPoint preserves the result, blocks false completion, and requires review/re-entry.

git.note: Release-candidate commit and CI run are recorded after final verification.
